instructions: In a bowl, stir the tarhana powder into 1 cup of the cold broth until it's a thick paste. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until it darkens a shade.
Add the minced garlic, paprika and mint. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the tarhana paste, the remaining 3 cups of broth and the salt. Whisk until there are no lumps.
Bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch on the bottom, until it thickens.
Break the vermicelli into short pieces and add it. Cook for 6 minutes, until tender. If the soup gets thicker than a cream soup, stir in a splash of water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Cooking Gorgeous (5 out of 5 from 2 votes, so below the 20 ratings needed) and Cup of Yum give the same soup: tarhana powder soaked, then simmered with butter, garlic, tomato paste, paprika, dried mint and a little vermicelli. Neither says when the vermicelli goes in, so it goes in for the last 6 minutes. Broth is vegetable to keep it vegetarian. Tarhana powder comes from Turkish or Middle Eastern grocers and online, and some brands are salty, so taste before adding more salt.
